response.markdown_report:
**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Positive–negative margins measure discrimination against supplied negatives. Their scale does not establish calibrated relevance or HR@10. (2) Existing probes never perturb histories. They therefore cannot test the diagnosis that older interactions outweigh coherent recent behavior. (3) Positionwise training scores do not verify inference readout. Left-padded histories require the final nonpadding position, never `count−1`.

**Insights from related work.** (1) NextItNet expands temporal coverage through dilated causal convolutions [1]. Architectural reach nevertheless differs from measured reliance on distant events. (2) Interaction-removal research reports greater sensitivity to recent training events [2]. Frozen-model inference perturbations require separate measurement because they answer a different question. (3) Usage-centric intent research distinguishes intended use from superficial product similarity [3]. Titles and descriptions support tentative evidence, but cannot establish satisfaction, compatibility, or unmet needs.

**Directions and framework.** Organize diagnosis along three axes: structural correctness, temporal reliance, and semantic evidence. Their corresponding observations are readout/receptive-field checks, paired prediction changes, and text-supported relation labels. Missing evidence must remain unknown; these axes measure model behavior and available evidence rather than latent user intent.

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/future potential/code difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Position-preserving lag ablation [1,2] | 4/7/3 | Simple, auditable evidence of temporal reliance | Masking introduces distribution shift; methodological novelty is modest |
| Train with occasional contiguous older-prefix dropout [1,2] | 4/6/4 | Tests a feasible recency regularizer within NextItNet | Can remove useful long-range evidence; benefit is unproven |
| Abstaining title/description relation audit [3] | 5/6/6 | Separates specific textual support from broad similarity | Sparse descriptions and twenty feedback users limit validation |

**Selected idea: position-preserving lag diagnosis.** At 0% research progress, first establish whether the proposed temporal failure occurs. Freeze each category’s single corrected NextItNet and compare intact histories with contiguous lag bands replaced by padding IDs without repacking. Report paired target-rank changes, hit@10 changes, and top-10 overlap separately from the unchanged host selection metric. Record counts and stratify by history length and receptive-field coverage. These are sensitivity measurements, not causal measurements of user intent.

```text
for sequence, positive, negative in bounded_training_batches:
    locate final nonpadding position
    score intact sequence and supplied candidates
    for lag_band in predefined_bands:
        mask band without moving remaining items
        recompute features and paired score changes
aggregate measurements, counts, definitions, and missing reasons
```

Use training-loader margins when validation candidates are unavailable; omit rank metrics rather than substitute invented values. Compute receptive-field span by counting every temporal convolution. Adapt masking to the actual backbone so padding behavior is explicit. Preserve `DiagnosisProbe`, `run_full_diagnosis`, `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt`, and all ModelView hooks. This diagnostic leaves training seeds, splits, routing, checkpoints, and predictor architecture unchanged; any later regularizer must update training and the embedded predictor consistently.

idea.description: Add a position-preserving lag-ablation diagnostic to the family-specific NextItNet adapter, measuring how masking predefined history bands changes the predictions of each category’s single trained model.
idea.motivation: The qualitative feedback suggests excessive reliance on broad or stale interests, but existing embedding and margin probes cannot establish temporal reliance. A small diagnostic provides evidence before spending the search budget on architecture changes.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Use view.model in evaluation mode under no_grad and restore its previous mode afterward. Use log2feats and predict_score; select the actual final nonpadding index and exclude empty histories. Keep item_emb compatibility. Mask contiguous lag bands without repacking and document the backbone’s padding behavior. Distinguish unavailable measurements from numeric zero, return observation counts and metric_definitions, and keep unavailable category metadata empty. Use loader-provided positives and negatives for training diagnostics; validation rank measurements require authorized fixed validation candidates and remain separate from host model selection. Preserve one checkpoint per category, all four routes, seeds, and the pinned evaluation protocol.
idea.pseudocode:
save training mode; model.eval()
with no_grad():
  for _, sequence, positive, negative in bounded(train_loader):
    valid = sequence != 0
    last = maximum valid position per row
    skip empty rows and positions without positive targets
    candidates = stack(positive_at_last, negative_at_last)
    intact = view.predict_score(gather(view.log2feats(sequence), last), candidates)
    for band in predefined_lag_bands:
      edited = sequence.clone()
      edited[valid positions in band relative to last] = 0
      changed = view.predict_score(gather(view.log2feats(edited), last), candidates)
      record paired margin change and observed counts
restore training mode
return {metrics: aggregate_or_missing(), metric_definitions: explicit_definitions}
# Interpreter prompt includes measured metrics, definitions, counts, and limitations.

originality.positive: Combines NextItNet receptive-field analysis with position-preserving temporal probes and an explicit missing-evidence contract.
originality.negative: Ablation and temporal sensitivity analysis are established techniques; novelty lies mainly in their task-specific integration.

future_potential.positive: Can guide targeted recency regularization while separating structural limitations from weak use of accessible history.
future_potential.negative: Diagnostic sensitivity may not predict improvements in validation HR@10 or reflect users’ actual reasons for choosing items.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires no additional fitted model and can operate through existing ModelView hooks on bounded batches.
code_difficulty.negative: Padding semantics, receptive-field accounting, and alignment of target positions require careful implementation.

related_work.title: NextItNet: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: Uses residual dilated causal convolutions for sequential recommendation.
Provides the architectural basis for calculating temporal receptive-field coverage.
limitations: Architectural receptive-field coverage does not establish actual reliance on distant interactions or identify user intent.

related_work.title: Interaction-removal study and finite rank-biased overlap
contributions: The supplied research summary reports greater accuracy degradation after removing recent training interactions.
Introduces finite rank-biased overlap for comparing finite recommendation lists.
limitations: Training-data removal findings do not directly establish the effects of inference-time masking on a frozen NextItNet.

related_work.title: Usage-centric Intent Understanding
contributions: Examines intended use beyond rigid product categories and ambiguous descriptive properties.
Motivates distinguishing specific textual evidence from broad semantic similarity.
limitations: Does not validate task-specific recommendation proxies or establish compatibility and satisfaction from interaction histories.
